local_takeaway: Segment-level or composition-level mimicry of natural protein chemistry can guide heteropolymer design when direct sequence control is unavailable.
Composition drift during polymerization means feed ratios are design variables but may not equal final chain composition, motivating conservative claims from formulation-only data.

Wet adhesion is fundamentally constrained by water-screened interactions; catechol/aromatic and balanced charged functionality are plausible levers, but strong underwater adhesion still requires integrated formulation and network mechanics.
